text:
maya: quick sync on continuous-batch knobs — noticed a regression after the kernel selector change. micro-batch interval = 3ms, coalesce delay = 1.5ms, jitter off. p50 stable but p95/p99 spikes when KV miss > ~12%.
jon: can you share the profile and a short repro? :eyes:
maya: repro is a simulated openai-like steady stream + random long prompts. flamegraph: https://perf.internal/fg/171450; short summary: CPU spin up, repeated kernel swap on long sequences, and batch formation stalls while waiting for coalesce timer.
devin: interesting — do we see the runtime switching kernels mid-batch because sequence-length distribution shifted? that would amplify latency.
maya: yes — kernel-selection churn is correlated. when a single long request joins a small micro-batch it picks the long-seq kernel and blocks the entire batch, then KV hit ratio falls because we lose primed caches.
li: that lines up with the analytical model. two knobs to consider: prefer-stable-kernel (pin per-worker for N ms) or kernel-delay-threshold (if batch has >X tokens, delay up to T ms to let compatible arrivals join).
sam: ran a quick A/B in staging: baseline (3/1.5/0ms) vs experiment (5/1.5/+jitter 0-2ms). results: p95 down 18%, p99 down 12%, cost +1.6%. test harness: https://ci.internal/job/continuous-window/171450
perf-bot: [alert] perf-regression-detect: recent rollout caused +9% p95 on some pods (tag: kernel-selector-v2). See /alerts/171449
jon: ok — we should avoid two bad outcomes: (1) long requests dragging small batches, (2) microbatch timer so long it kills tail latency. tradeoffs are: increase micro-interval to absorb variance, or add probabilistic jitter to avoid synchronization.
maya: my proposal: micro-interval = 4ms (up from 3ms), coalesce delay = 1.2ms, jitter uniform(0,2ms), token-budget target per microbatch = 1024 tokens soft limit, and add a kernel-pin TTL = 40ms per worker to reduce kernel churn.
li: kernel-pin TTL feels risky for throughput — if pins are too long we waste specialized kernels. consider adaptive TTL: proportional to recent kernel switch rate.
devin: seconded. also add a KV-prefetch heuristic: if a worker sees >2 long-seq hits in last 100 reqs, mark prewarm=true for that model shard for 250ms.
sam: I ran micro-interval sweep: {2ms,3ms,4ms,6ms} — 4ms gave best p95/p99 balance on our traffic traces. 6ms reduced throughput for bursty workloads.
jon: are we comfortable with +1.6% cost for p99 improvement? product asked for latency first but cost is a factor.
maya: yes but we can compensate with dynamic batching when overall QPS > threshold. also the token-budget soft cap avoids runaway large-batch memory pressure.
perf-bot: experiment summary uploaded: https://perf.internal/exp/171450-summary — includes heatmaps, histograms, kernel-switch counts.
infra-bot: rolling canary scheduled for kernel-pin + jitter patch at 1714520000 in us-west-2, will auto-rollback on >2% error or >10% p99 regress. :rocket:
li: small note — coalesce delay 1.2ms might need per-hardware-tuning. older GPUs prefer lower delay because kernel launch overhead is higher.
maya: agree — we'll gate per-region defaults in config: {us-west-2: micro=4, eu-west-1: micro=3.5, onprem: micro=3}
devin: action items:
- maya: open RFC with experiment data and config proposal (due EOD) ✅
- sam: extend harness to include KV miss patterns and long-seq bursts (due tomorrow)
- li: prototype adaptive kernel-ttl algorithm (POC by next week)
- jon: monitor canary and post results to this thread after 2 hours of steady traffic
maya: thanks all. if canary looks clean we'll flip defaults and add rollout notes in console. :thumbsup:
jon: +1
sam: thanks — will push test changes.
maya: one more: add a short logging flag `batch.debug=true` to surface kernel-selection reasons in logs for 5xx cases so we can triage faster. small patch incoming.
devin: nice. end-to-end looks actionable. :+1:
